post.title: Animated Code Walkthrough
post.hook: Edit a code file, and the video re-renders itself in the preview.
post.summary: A Remotion project that turns code snippets into an animated, step by step code video with token transitions and a progress bar. It is a one commit starter, set up and wired but not yet pushed far.
post.writeup:
## What it is
A Remotion video project, scaffolded on 2026-01-25, built to animate code. Snippets live in `public/` (code1.tsx to code4.swift), and each one becomes a step in the video.

## Why it exists
Code walkthrough clips usually mean screen recording and manual editing. Here the video is React, so changing a snippet changes the video.

## How it works
`Main.tsx` splits the total duration evenly across the snippets using `Series`, with a 30 frame transition between steps. `CodeTransition.tsx` uses Code Hike's token transitions to morph one highlighted snippet into the next, and waits for layout before rendering via `useDelayRender`. `ProgressBar.tsx` draws one bar per step and fills the current one as frames advance. Fonts come from Roboto Mono at size 40.

A small component, `ReloadOnCodeChange`, hashes the names and modified times of every static file starting with "code". When the hash changes in the Studio, it calls `reevaluateComposition`, so edits show up without a manual refresh.

## What is in the folder
The sample snippets walk through a tiny `user` object: a type hover, then a TypeScript error on a missing `location` property, then the fix, then a Swift version. The project also carries image assets (dashboard and agent capability screenshots, logos) and two mp4 files.

## Stack
Remotion 4.0.409, React 19.2.3, codehike 1.0.4, Zod 3.22.3, TypeScript 5.9.3. Render with `npx remotion render`; preview with `npm run dev`. The config sets JPEG frames and overwrites output.

## Status and open questions
There is a single commit and the README is still the stock template. No finished render is documented. Open questions: which snippets make the final cut, and whether the screenshots in `public/` are meant to be combined with the code steps in one video.
